sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Fluorescence microscopy in M10 melanoma cells: Lang-YFP displayed an identical cellular distribution to wild-type Langerin (L4). Trafficking to Birbeck granule-associated compartments was unperturbed.
sites.rationale: CD207 is a type II single-pass TM protein; its C-terminus (residue 328, P) is extracellular and is the only extracellular terminus. The ledger (L3, confirmed by L4) reports a full-length, membrane-anchored Lang-YFP construct with YFP at the 'C-terminal luminal/extracellular position' that recapitulates wild-type Langerin cellular distribution. Because there is exactly one extracellular terminus, the junction is unambiguously after residue 328; insert_after_residue is topology-derived, not chosen. The tag is 264 residues from the TM boundary, well clear of any constraint. Lang-YFP: full-length, membrane-anchored CD207 (Langerin) with YFP fused at the C-terminal luminal/extracellular end, expressed in M10 melanoma cells. CD207 is a type II transmembrane protein (intracellular N-terminus residues 1–43, TM 44–64, extracellular C-terminus 65–328); the C-terminus is the sole extracellular terminus, so the junction is unambiguously residue 328. The paper names the position as 'C-terminal luminal/extracellular' but gives no residue number; position is computed from topology landmarks.

sources.claim: We previously used a Langerin-YFP fusion protein having a C-terminal luminal YFP tag to dynamically decipher the molecular and cellular processes which accompany the traffic of Langerin.

literature_notes: CD207 (Langerin) is a type II single-pass transmembrane protein with an intracellular N-terminus (1–43), TM helix (44–64), and a large extracellular C-terminal domain (65–328). The ledger contains four lines, all from PMC3618057. L1 and L2 describe YFP-Lang (YFP at the N-terminal cytoplasmic end) — intracellular, not a surface tag site, and L4 shows it perturbs trafficking. L3 and L4 describe Lang-YFP (YFP at the C-terminal luminal/extracellular position) — the only extracellular terminus, tolerated with identical WT distribution. No ledger line supports any internal extracellular loop insertion. evidence_type is 'published tag insertion in the same loop or domain' rather than 'at this exact site' because the paper names the position descriptively ('C-terminal luminal/extracellular') without a residue number; the junction at 328 is topology-derived. cited_tag_residue is set to 328 as the computed junction.

literature_other_positions.note: YFP-Lang places YFP at the N-terminal cytoplasmic end of full-length Langerin (residues 1–43 are intracellular); L4 shows this construct coalesces in enlarged structures, indicating perturbed trafficking — both intracellular and function-perturbing.
